news.title:
PL Capital favors Adani Ports, Adani Power, and Adani Enterprises for strong growth potential in India's infrastructure and energy sectors.
Adani Ports leads in logistics with 26% of India's seaborne trade, while Adani Power targets 42 GW capacity by FY32, and AEL drives growth in diversified infrastructure.

5 Adani stocks, including Adani Power, hit 52-week highs; Adani Power surpasses Infosys in market cap at ₹4.77T.
Adani Enterprises plans value unlocking via demergers; SBI MF acquired 0.5% stake worth ₹1,435 crore recently.
Upcoming dividend of ₹1.30 per share
news.body: Eligible shareholders must have bought the stock before 12 June 2026. Payment date: 24 July 2026. Payout ratio is a comfortable 1.7% but the company is not cash flow positive. The company last paid an ordinary dividend in March 2016. The average dividend yield among industry peers is 0.2%.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: Revenues exceed analysts expectations while EPS lags behind
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹75.66 (up from ₹58.90 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹1.00t (up 2.6% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹92.3b (up 33% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 9.2% (up from 7.1% in FY 2025). Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 2.9%. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates by 18%. Revenue is forecast to grow 23% p.a. on average during the next 2 years, compared to a 6.0% growth forecast for the Trade Distributors industry in Asia. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 52% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 6% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.

news.title: Adani Enterprises Limited (BSE:512599)  completed the acquisition of  24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures Limited (NSEI:JPPOWER) from Jaiprakash Associates Limited (BSE:532532) for INR 29.9 billion.
news.body:
Adani Enterprises Limited (BSE:512599) agreed to acquire 24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures Limited (NSEI:JPPOWER) from Jaiprakash Associates Limited (BSE:532532) for INR 29.9 billion on March 17, 2026. Adani Enterprises Limited entered into share purchase agreement to acquire 24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures Limited from Jaiprakash Associates Limited on May 21, 2026. A cash consideration of INR 29.94 billion will be paid by Adani Enterprises Limited.

The transaction is expected to close in 90 days from March 17, 2026. The transaction was approved by National Company Law Tribunal on March 17, 2026 and from Competition Commission of India on August 26, 2025.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues exceed analyst expectations
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹46.78 (up from ₹0.50 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹248.2b (up 8.6% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹56.3b (up ₹55.7b from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 23% (up from 0.3% in 3Q 2025). Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 4.2%. Earnings per share (EPS) also surpassed analyst estimates significantly. Revenue is forecast to grow 22% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 5.6% growth forecast for the Trade Distributors industry in Asia. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 56% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 1% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.

news.title: New major risk - Revenue and earnings growth
news.body: Earnings are forecast to decline by an average of 2.6% per year for the foreseeable future. This is considered a major risk. Ultimately, shareholders want to see a good return on their investment and that generally comes from sharing in the company's profits. If profits are expected to decline, then in most cases the share price will decline over time as well. In addition, if the company pays dividends it will also likely need to reduce or cut them, striking a dual blow to total shareholder returns. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Major Risks Interest payments are not well covered by earnings (1.7x net interest cover).
